items.title: David Marskell, Frank Boutzis, Deb MacLatchy and Paul Salvini from THEMUSEUM
notes:
D. Marskell and F. Boutzis appeared before the Committee and provided a presentation on behalf of THEMUSEUM. A copy of the presentation is appended to the original minutes. They highlighted its achievements, vision, and mission. They discussed the organization's potential community impact and commitment to sustainability.

Committee members inquired about funding sources and THEMUSEUM's role in the community. D. Marskell emphasized the significance of both, highlighting the crucial collaboration with businesses.

items.title: Raechele Lovell and Arsen Stepanyan, Region of Waterloo Arts Fund
notes:
R. Lovell and A. Stepanyan appeared before the Committee on behalf of the Region of Waterloo Arts Fund, expressing their advocacy for the continued support of arts and culture within the Region. They shared concerns regarding delays in implementing equity initiatives within the Arts Fund by the Region administration and finance department. They emphasized the crucial role of arts and culture in the community.

In response to a question from the Committee, R. Lovell addressed the delays in equity initiatives since her appointment as Chair of the board.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
COR-CFN-24-002, 2024 Community Capacity Building Fund Overview
notes:
Craig Dyer, Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer opened the report by discussing the recommendations, emphasizing the accomplishments of the Community Capacity Building Fund. He outlined that during the 2024 plan and budget process, Council allocated $1M to support this initiative. Fauzia Baig, Director of Equity, Diversity & Inclusion, further elaborated on the presentation, emphasizing how the fund aligns with community needs and is structured to empower local initiatives and grassroots organizations for sustainable growth.

In response to a question from the Committee, F. Baig addressed the program's outreach in Cambridge and underscored the significance of prioritizing efforts in inclusion, outreach, and accessibility.

F. Baig addressed the Committee's inquiries about supporting youth groups through the program, acknowledging their reported sense of disconnection from society. She emphasized the significance of addressing youth needs and highlighted potential opportunities for collaboration with youth communities.

items.title: COR-CFN-24-003, Key Cultural Institutions 2024 Funding Allocations
notes:
C. Dyer discussed the report, noting that this grant stream is one of several approved funding envelopes through the budget process. Over the next few months, recommendations will be presented based on equitable allocation among four organizations.

Councillor J. Erb brought forward an amendment to the motion. 

Councillor B. Vrbanovic proposed an amendment to that amendment.

The Committee members discussed the amendment. In response to a question, Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development & Legislative Services, stated that staff regularly engage in discussions with area municipalities regarding funding programs for cultural institutions in the Region. These discussions are collaborative, and there's flexibility in arrangements as each budget cycle determines the funding allocation for programming. R. Regier further noted that staff bring back the report in August, as they are currently in the process of recruiting the staff in the Region who will be participating in this work.

Responding to questions, C. Dyer mentioned that they are currently in the process of finalizing the year-end 2023 statements, so he doesn't have an exact figure for the tax stabilization reserve at the end of the year. He estimates it to be around $12 million. Considering the commitments made through the 2024 budget and including the figure from the motion by Councillor Erb, there is a significant amount committed against that reserve fund. This is the most strain the reserve has experienced. If something arises in 2024 requiring immediate funding, the council's flexibility will be limited going into the 2025 budget year.

C. Dyer concluded with final remarks, offering clarity on the motion by adjusting the numbers to align with the proposed amendment's intent. He confirmed that staff have revised the figures in the motion to reflect the amendment.

Members of the Committee discussed the broader allocation of various funding streams and emphasized the importance of communication with area municipalities, which may need to be involved in these discussions.

items.title: Other Business
notes: Councillor D. Craig raised concerns regarding the funding model moving forward, emphasizing a perceived disparity in funding among groups in Cambridge. He expressed a desire for this issue to be addressed in future discussions and integrated into ongoing dialogue. Additionally, he inquired about the rules of debate regarding delegation time and advocated for leniency. In response, Will Short, Director, Council & Administrative Services/Regional Clerk, explained that the current Procedural By-law provides the Chair with flexibility regarding debate time, however there is a risk of complaints if one delegation is given more time than another. He clarified that delegation time is based on timely registration.

motions.item_title: COR-CFN-24-003, Key Cultural Institutions 2024 Funding Allocations
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2024 allocations under the Key Cultural Institutions grant program as outlined in COR-CFN-24-003 dated February 6, 2024: 1. Approve the 2024 allocation of $840,603 under the Key Cultural Institutions grant program as set out below: Kitchener Waterloo Art Gallery - $100,000 Canadian Clay and Glass Gallery - $93,587 Drayton Entertainment - $261,291 THEMUSEUM - $385,725; 2. Fund the additional costs (in excess of the 2024 Budget provision) of $493,450 from the Tax Stabilization Reserve in 2024; 3. Direct staff to include an incremental $493,450 in the Preliminary 2025 Base Budget funded from the property tax levy; and 4. Direct staff to review the KCI program and funding model with the area municipal working group in 2024, and provide an update to Regional Council in 2024 so that there is clarity in advance of 2025 funding requests
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2024 allocations under the Key Cultural Institutions grant program as outlined in COR-CFN-24-003 dated February 6, 2024:

 

1. Approve the 2024 allocation of $840,603 under the Key Cultural Institutions grant program as set out below:

    1. Kitchener Waterloo Art Gallery - $100,000
    2. Canadian Clay and Glass Gallery - $93,587
    3. Drayton Entertainment - $261,291
    4. THEMUSEUM - $385,725;

2. Fund the additional costs (in excess of the 2024 Budget provision) of $493,450 from the Tax Stabilization Reserve in 2024;

3. Direct staff to include an incremental $493,450 in the Preliminary 2025 Base Budget funded from the property tax levy; and

4. Direct staff to review the KCI program and funding model with the area municipal working group in 2024, and provide an update to Regional Council in 2024 so that there is clarity in advance of 2025 funding requests

motions.item_title: COR-CFN-24-003, Key Cultural Institutions 2024 Funding Allocations
motions.text: AMENDMENT: THAT the funding for THEMUSEUM in 2024 be set at its previous level of $385,725 THAT the additional shortfall of funding ($93,450) in the 2024 KCI grant budget also be funded through the tax stabilization reserve fund AND FURTHER THAT staff be directed to review the KCI program and funding model with the area municipal working group in 2024, and provide an update to Regional Council in 2024 so that there is clarity in advance of 2025 funding requests.
motions.text_html:
AMENDMENT:

  • THAT the funding for THEMUSEUM in 2024 be set at its previous level of $385,725
  • THAT the additional shortfall of funding ($93,450) in the 2024 KCI grant budget also be funded through the tax stabilization reserve fund

  • AND FURTHER THAT staff be directed to review the KCI program and funding model with the area municipal working group in 2024, and provide an update to Regional Council in 2024 so that there is clarity in advance of 2025 funding requests.

motions.text: That the meeting adjourn at 11:05 a.m.
